design.summary:
Build H1 as one harness-only change, which is the long-deferred item M1 in docs/shiploop-callback-typos-plan-2026-10-04.md. Do not build the whole list in the candidate text. metrics.collect() should feed Claude tool_use and tool_result blocks through the single classifier the Grok tool_call path already uses (glue_reasons, tmp_writes, failure_line, stage tool calls, asked-person). The existing shapes are reused: model_glue, shiploop_failures, tmp_writes, stages[].tool_calls and the Codex per-stage context map {calls, peak, peakPct}. Only a few things are new.

Three details matter:
- Claude commands are multi-line shell with `RUN=...` assignments, so paths are expanded per command first (`expand_variables`).
- Refusals mostly sit behind exit 0 because the model pipes the CLI through head, grep or sed. They are detected by their line-anchored text, not by the exit code.
- `ShipLoop workspace blocked:` is a third refusal prefix that REFUSAL_LINE does not cover.

New record-only block `tool_use`:
- `calls`, `by_tool`, `result_chars`.
- `scratch_scripts`: files the model wrote that are invoked and either live under scratch/ or wrap the CLI.
- `packets`: `on_disk`, `printed`, `read`.

Two tiny host-independent fixes: `script_verifications.not_green` and `improve_reviews.identical`.

Dropped:
- No Claude compaction counter. No recorded stream has a compaction event, and the only context shrinks in 15 runs are session starts.
- No Claude truncated_outputs, knowledge_reads or cancelled_tool_calls.
- No exporter edits. The unmodified exporter already consumes the new fields: I ran export.py on a copy of the Battleship run with an edited metrics.json and got refusals 5, glue 1, per-stage context, and the facts.md lines.

A prototype on all 15 recorded Claude runs reproduced every lens figure that was hand-mined from events.jsonl.
design.for_against:
FOR:
- Every round-1 lens hand-mined events.jsonl for the same facts, because metrics.py CLAUDE_BLIND and CLAUDE_TOOL_BLOCKS leave stage_tool_calls, shiploop_failures, model_glue and tmp_writes unmeasured. LEARNINGS.md item 7 already admitted "the failure metric is blind for Claude" and planned M1.
- The prototype reproduces the hand figures exactly. Battleship: 120 tool calls (115 Bash, 4 Read, 1 Edit); 222,269 result chars; 5 refusals; 44 packet files of 1,707,162 B on disk; 4 Read calls (2 whole, 28,595 and 21,636 chars); 23 shell commands naming packets/ (64,249 chars); sub.sh run 30 times. Checkers: 209,381 chars, 45 files of 1,737,466 B.
- It surfaces a pattern: 14 of 15 recorded Claude runs wrote at least one invoked helper script that wraps the CLI. model_glue alone shows 0 to 3 because writes into run/scratch, inbox and notes are MODEL_INPUT.
- Live progress.py picks it up too, since it calls collect() on each poll.
- It serves SPEC S-1, S-2, S-4, S-5 and S-7 evidence. It is record-only: no state key, no packet text, no engine file.

AGAINST:
- Five existing tests pin "Claude is blind" and must flip.
- shared_tmp_writes now includes Claude runs. That is intended: r1 Battleship wrote the shared /tmp/bs.pid.
- Counts are heuristic lower bounds. Variable expansion is line-leading assignments only, and a wrapper hides its verb.
- A larger parser is not worth it. The compaction proxy, truncated_outputs, knowledge_reads, tool-error counts, Write-tool glue and next-id extraction counts were all considered and dropped (see per_candidate).

per_candidate.change: One batch in test/shiploop_e2e/metrics.py (plus the print sites in run.py and progress.py), fixtures under docs/experiments/claude-tool-blocks-20261008/, tests in test/shiploop-e2e.test.py. Sub-parts below; the candidate's host-independent items are split out as H1d.

Claude tool_use/tool_result blocks go through the shared classifier. Failures are recorded by an anchored refusal line or by an `Exit code N` prefix on a command that names the ShipLoop CLI or a scratch script the model wrote; the verb comes from the command, `via <script>` for a wrapper, `unknown` otherwise; exit is null when the host did not show it. REFUSAL_LINE gains `workspace blocked`. CLAUDE_BLIND and CLAUDE_TOOL_BLOCKS are removed. Closes M1 and the Claude cells of LEARNINGS item 7.

New `tool_use` block {calls, by_tool, result_chars, scratch_scripts[{path, bytes, wraps_shiploop, runs}], packets{on_disk, printed, read}}, None with a reason in unmeasured['tool_use'] on other hosts. Answers 'packet bytes read vs printed' and 'scratch scripts written'.

Per-stage `context` {calls, peak, peakPct} for Claude from message ids and context_tokens, in the shape the exporter already reads for Codex. stages[].turns keeps its events-based definition (baselines.jsonl pins it).

Host-independent labels: script_verifications.not_green (records whose own `expect` is `red` or `a test ran`; 2 of the 'passed 10' in r1 Battleship) and improve_reviews.identical (consecutive review notes equal but for the digits in their first line: 1 in r1 Battleship, 3 of 3 children that needed a trivial pass in r1 Checkers). Drop 'bind-to-complete seconds for every child': planning.stages[].improve_seconds already covers the five planning children.

Claude compactions or any 'context drop' counter. No compact_boundary in 15 recorded Claude streams; the only in-stream context shrinks (6 older runs, e.g. 204,737 to 33,871) fall exactly at a `system/init` session start (a resume), not a compaction, and there is no positive control. Keep compactions unmeasured. The per-stage peak and peakPct are the context evidence; add the compact_boundary branch when a stream shows one (the existing metrics.py comment says the same).

Claude truncated_outputs (the `<\persisted-output>` marker, 9 results in older runs, none in the r1 runs), knowledge_reads (the model reads via shell, so a Read-tool-only list would be a misleading measured []), cancelled_tool_calls (no recorded Claude permission refusal), tool-error counts, Write-tool glue, next-id extraction counts. Each needs a second reader (run.host_truncations) or has no recorded positive.
Exporter and page edits: skills/shiploop-run-review is owned by another session. Hand off the proposed run fields instead (see risks).

changes.change: Move the body of the Grok `tool_call` branch (ASK_PERSON, calls[id]={t,command}, glue_reasons, tmp_writes, WRITE_TOOL /tmp targets) into note_call(t, id, tool, arg, command_expanded) and the failure branch into note_result(id, shown, exit). Call both from the existing `assistant` branch (each tool_use block; the existing Claude ASK_PERSON line goes) and a new `user` branch (each tool_result block, content str or text-part list as _tool_output does). Delete the CLAUDE_BLIND unmeasured marking. `reads`, cancelled and compactions stay Grok-only (the existing `if not grok` blanking). Claude's failure rule: a result with an anchored refusal line, or an `Exit code N` prefix on a ShipLoop-naming command; failure_line is given the text from the first refusal line on, so a model's own traceback earlier in the output does not become the recorded line (r1 Checkers: 'KeyError' vs 'Until Loop terminal packet is not complete').

shell_variables(command): assignments at a line start or after `;`, single/double/unquoted values with no command substitution, resolved against earlier ones, per command (variables did not carry across calls in any recorded run). expand_variables uses a `\$(?:\{(\w+)\}|(\w+))` substitution, not str.replace. claude_exit parses `\AExit code (\d+)`; this was validated: every Bash result with the prefix has is_error true and none without it does, across about 3,500 results in 15 runs. written_scripts: heredoc files (`cat|tee > PATH <<TAG ... TAG`, matched on the original text so `bytes` is the real body) whose expanded path is under /run/scratch/ or whose body matches SHIPLOOP_COMMAND / `scripts/shiploop`. invokes(path, shell_text): path at a command position or after an interpreter word, heredoc bodies removed, so `--result=PATH` data arguments do not count.

The prototype requires the command, or a wrapper's body, to match SHIPLOOP_COMMAND. 3. Fix variable expansion. In r1 Checkers idx 372 the quoted `sh -c '... R=$?; ...'` inside the command overrides the real `R=.../run`, so `$R/scratch/sub.sh` expands to `$?/scratch/sub.sh`. shell_variables as described (line-start or after `;`, last wins) hits this, and it loses a wrapper-submitted refusal and 3 sub.sh runs. Rule to add: an assignment whose value is still unresolved after expansion (`$?`, `$!`, `$(`, unknown variable) is not recorded. Add a test built from that recorded command. Tried here: the fix gives Checkers ih.sh 10 / sub.sh 29 / loopdone.sh 3 / loop.sh 1 per call (lens 10/30/4/1), so some misses remain; keep the count labelled a lower bound.
